hints: Picking the first 3 or the second 3 from [3,1,3] gives the same pick. How can you make sure equal values are only ever 'started' once at the same step?
Sort nums so equal values sit together, then backtrack with a start index. In one loop level, if nums[j] == nums[j-1] and j > start, skip it: that branch was already explored.

1. Sort nums.
  2. go(start): add a copy of the current pick to the answer (every node is a valid pick).
  3. Loop j from start to the end; skip if j > start and nums[j] == nums[j-1].
  4. Add nums[j], call go(j+1), then remove it.
  5. Call go(0) and return the answer.

approaches.name: Brute force + set
approaches.idea: Generate all 2<sup>n</sup> subsets, sort each, and keep only unseen ones in a set.

approaches.name: Optimal: sorted backtracking with skip
approaches.idea: Sort once and skip equal values at the same depth, so duplicates are never built.

explain: For [3,1,3], sorting gives [1,3,3]. Starting from the empty pick we record [], then try 1 (giving [1], [1,3], [1,3,3]), then the first 3 (giving [3], [3,3]); the second 3 at the top level is skipped because it equals its left neighbour. That yields exactly the 6 different picks. The skip uses j > start, not j > 0, so taking two 3s in a row (going deeper) is still allowed.
recognize: 'Return all sub-collections' + 'may contain repeated values' + 'no duplicates' → sort, then backtrack and skip equal values at the same depth.
